title: Inkwell Blog Platform
summary: A statically generated blog built to learn the Next.js App Router: dynamic routes, route groups, metadata, RSS and sitemaps.
body:
Inkwell is a developer journal with honest notes on building web apps from Nigeria, written for slow data and small phones. It’s my first Next.js project, so every route was chosen to practise a specific routing feature.

**What it does**

- Posts are Markdown files with typed frontmatter, so there’s no database.
- The whole blog is pre-rendered at build time, including paginated listing pages and tag, category and author pages.
- Post pages have a table of contents, a reading progress bar, links to previous and next posts, and related posts based on shared tags.
- Search runs on the server, and the query stays in the URL.
- Each post gets its own social share image, plus an RSS feed, a sitemap and robots.txt.
- It has light and dark mode with no flash on load, and works down to 360px.

**What I learned**

- How the file system defines routes in the App Router, including dynamic segments and route groups.
- How `generateStaticParams` and `dynamicParams` decide which pages exist and which return a 404.
- When a component needs to be a Client Component, and why most of them don’t.
